content: To see what is right and not do it is the supreme want of courage.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Jian yi bu wei, wu yong ye (见义不为，无勇也) — Analects of Confucius (Book II)
explanation: Moral clarity without action is merely cowardly hypocrisy. It costs nothing to nod in agreement with virtue in the safety of your study; courage is stepping into the arena and defending the truth when personal comfort, status, or popularity are at stake.
practicalInsight: If you witness an injustice or someone being mistreated today, do not look away. Speak up with calm, resolute integrity.
reflectionPrompt: Where are you silently tolerating a wrong simply because speaking up feels inconvenient or awkward?
